paper_title: Constraining Axion Dark Matter with Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
suggested_experiment_name: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraint on axion dark matter
coupling_convention: d_n in GeV^-1 (neutron EDM coupling to axion, as plotted on y-axis labeled 'g_d [GeV^-1]')
notes: Paper constrains axion dark matter via BBN effects on neutron-proton mass difference. The primary exclusion is presented in (m_a, g_d) space where g_d ≈ 2.4×10^-16 e·cm / f_a [GeV]. The paper states the BBN bound as f_a·m_a > 1.3×10^-9 GeV^2 (for m_a > 10^-16 eV) and provides a modified bound for m_a ≪ 10^-16 eV. The coupling g_d is defined in equation (16) as the amplitude of oscillating neutron EDM induced by axion DM. The paper uses a local DM density ρ_DM ≈ 0.3 GeV/cm^3 in the context of oscillating EDM experiments (CASPEr). The exclusion is mass-independent over the range shown (horizontal line in g_d-m_a plane), reflecting the BBN constraint that depends on the product f_a·m_a rather than individual values. The coupling values emitted represent the g_d parameter from equation (16), which has units GeV^-2 as shown in Figure 1. Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because: (1) the paper's primary result is on f_a·m_a product rather than individual (m_a, coupling) pairs, requiring interpretation; (2) the coupling type is AxionEDM but the paper frames it as a constraint on g_d which relates to the EDM amplitude; (3) the mass-independent nature of the bound requires sentinel encoding.
